title: Hannah Yeoh told to sign order document despite not wanting to, after opposing Najib's house arrest
text:
Hannah Yeoh told to sign order document despite not wanting to, after opposing Najib's house arrest Friday 20 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Highlight Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 18): Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh did not want to sign the house arrest order for Datuk Seri Najib Razak, but was told she had to, minutes of the Sept 18 meeting of the Pardons Board showed.
 Yeoh, who had opposed granting another clemency for the former prime minister, suggested during the September meeting that another officer, such as the Cabinet secretary, sign the conditional pardon due to significant political implication and impact to the government.
 However, some members of the Pardons Board advised that it would be inappropriate for non-members or non-participants of the meeting to sign the order.
 The Yang di-Pertuan Agong ultimately decided that Yeoh must sign the order in her capacity as Federal Territories minister.
 The meeting minutes offer a rare glimpse into the Pardons Board proceedings and considerations that went into the second clemency for Najib, who was convicted of grand corruption.
 At the meeting, Yeoh expressed the same view as Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, who objected to the house arrest. He was of the view that Najib should serve out his sentence in prison.
 “This decision will affect the government, especially political stability, economy, investment and the country’s image internationally,” Mohd Dusuki had said during the Pardons Board meeting.
 Yeoh is a deputy secretary general of the Democratic Action Party that has been among the staunchest critics of Najib over the theft of billions from 1MDB.
 Umno managed to raise and paid the RM50 million fine on Najib’s behalf earlier this month to meet one of the requirements of the house arrest. He has since been transferred from the Kajang Prison to his home in Langgak Duta and will stay there until Aug 23, 2028.
 Najib has been in custody since August 2022 after being found guilty of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving SRC International Sdn Bhd, a former subsidiary of government company 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
 The original sentence was for 12 years in jail and a RM210 million fine before the punishment was lessened in 2024 by the previous king, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'yatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
 Najib was subsequently sentenced to another 15 years’ imprisonment in December 2025 after being found guilty for a more serious crime at 1MDB, although he is appealing against the decision. The sentence is to run after he finishes his SRC jail term on Aug 23, 2028.
